judgments.reasoning_cat1: It lists six specific contents for a Potential Claim notice and a residual duty to give 'such additional information and cooperation as it may reasonably require', made a condition precedent — the residual duty is open but reasonableness-bounded.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It supports VI.A and echoes the cooperation duty in V.C and the condition precedent in VIII.H; I found no provision that contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'as soon as practicable, but in no event later than sixty (60) days after such Claim is first made' is a definite outer limit paired with a soft standard, the usual formulation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its sixty-day clock runs from when the subsequent Claim is made, whereas Section I caps reporting at sixty days after the Policy Period expires, so a Claim maturing long after expiry is treated differently by the two provisions. That is a concrete conflict with the Insuring Agreement's proviso.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Notice is 'deemed to be received and effective upon actual receipt ... or one day following the date such notices are sent, whichever is earlier', which produces the odd result that notice can be effective before receipt, and the cross-reference reads 'Item 711'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Item 11 splits claim notices from all other notices, and Section I and VI impose the operative reporting deadlines, so the deeming rule here directly affects whether reporting was timely under those provisions. The mis-citation and the deeming rule together are worth checking against Item 11.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The paragraph is internally strained: entities become Subsidiaries only if their headcount is under ten percent, but the 'notwithstanding' paragraph gives ninety days' cover only where headcount grows above 110 percent, leaving the middle band unaddressed, and 'as for a period of ninety (90) days' is mangled.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: III.U defines Subsidiary by reference back to this subsection and Exclusion A.6 denies cover for pre-acquisition acts, so the gap between the ten percent and 110 percent tests has to be resolved across three provisions. That is a genuine whole-instrument problem.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The change-of-control run-off is stated in definite terms with express carve-outs for receivership and debtor-in-possession status; little to construe lexically.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It says coverage 'shall not be cancellable by the Parent Company', which qualifies VIII.C.1's unrestricted right of the Parent Company to cancel — a limited but identifiable tension. Otherwise it fits III.O and VIII.A.3.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two lines with a clear cut-off tied to the date the organisation ceased to be a Subsidiary; 'termination of the Policy' rather than 'Policy Period' is a small imprecision.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It complements Exclusion A.6 (no cover for acts while not a Subsidiary) and III.U; no contradiction located, though 'termination of the Policy' must be read with III.P.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'All such statements are the basis of this Policy' combined with a severability regime and a broad imputation list (including 'human resources manager or risk manager') leaves scope for argument about whose knowledge counts, and the text is mechanically garbled.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It incorporates the Application into the Policy while VIII.K declares the Policy the entire agreement, and III.A defines Application expansively — those three provisions have to be reconciled. A modest but real integration tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The enumeration is mechanically broken (items rendered as 'N', 'an', '8') and item 1 gives the Parent Company an unqualified right to cancel with no minimum notice.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is the provision III.P's cross-reference should have pointed to, VIII.A.2 says coverage 'shall not be cancellable by the Parent Company' after a change of control, and II.C makes the ERP right depend on who cancels or non-renews. Those three connections give a court something to reconcile.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The excess wording is confined to 'Loss arising from any Third Party Claim' yet closes with 'in all other events, this Policy is intended to provide primary insurance', a sweeping residual whose reach against other insurance is debatable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Third Party Claim cover itself depends on Item 7 in the Declarations, so if that election is not clearly made the excess clause has no obvious field of operation; otherwise nothing contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One sentence, worldwide, with no qualifying language.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It matches the worldwide references in III.F, III.Q and IV.A.11; no conflict found, though the currency clause (VIII.F) is its natural companion.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Specific conversion mechanic tied to a named publication and identified dates; nothing open.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It fits VIII.E (Territory) and III.L (Loss) without friction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard subrogation with a broad cooperation duty ('everything necessary'), which is conventional rather than ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits comfortably with V.C's cooperation duty and VIII.H; no conflicting provision located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'full compliance with all the terms of this Policy' as a condition precedent is an absolute formulation that courts often have to soften or construe, though its meaning is plain on the page.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It reinforces the condition-precedent language in VI.B and the notice provisions; nothing in the Policy contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short, symmetrical bankruptcy clause with nothing elastic in the wording.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It matches III.O's inclusion of a debtor in possession and VIII.A.2's statement that receivership is not an acquisition; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It appoints the Parent Company as agent for all notices with a parenthetical exception for 'the giving of notice to apply for any Extended Reporting Period', a carve-out whose practical operation is not spelled out.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: II.C says the ERP election notice is 'given by the Insured' and gives the right to the Policyholder or the Insured Individuals, so the carve-out here must be read with II.C and VII; that is a small but identifiable interaction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It combines a written-endorsement-only variation clause with an entire-agreement statement and a non-waiver clause, each in definite terms; the non-waiver sentence is oddly two-sided but clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The entire-agreement statement sits against VIII.B, which incorporates the Application and all submitted statements into the Policy, and against the Declarations and Item 12 endorsements — a nameable integration tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short interpretive rule stating headings form no part of the terms; nothing to construe in itself.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Several provisions are cross-referenced by section heading (for example III.P's reference to a lettered subsection), so disclaiming headings can complicate those references, but the clause is standard.
